grounds.point: Dr. Vijay Kumar was the tenant of the disputed shop.
grounds.explanation: The supplied target source expressly identifies Dr. Vijay Kumar as tenant of shop No. 2855 and the respondent as its owner. This supplies the tenant-premises relationship required by the quoted Section 14(1)(b) formulation.

grounds.point: Dr. Vijay Kumar parted with possession of part of the shop to his sons.
grounds.explanation: The Rent Controller found separate portions, separate locking, and exclusive possession by the second and third appellants, and expressly concluded that the first appellant had parted with possession of their portion. The asserted joint-business explanation was rejected for lack of supporting financial records.

grounds.point: The qualifying parting with possession occurred on or after 9 June 1952.
grounds.explanation: The ejectment application was filed in 1965 and the Rent Controller later found that possession had been parted with, but the supplied target passages do not state when that transfer occurred. Those later procedural dates do not by themselves establish the statutory transfer-event date.

grounds.point: The landlord gave no written consent for the relevant parting with possession.
grounds.explanation: Counsel asserted that the first appellant permitted his sons to occupy half the shop, which concerns permission from the tenant. The supplied statutory wording requires written consent of the landlord, and no target passage establishes either the existence or absence of such written landlord consent for this transaction.

reason: The supplied record establishes tenancy and an express prior-court finding that Dr. Vijay Kumar parted with possession of part of the premises. The statutory timing condition and absence of written landlord consent remain unresolved on the supplied materials, so the fixed eviction ground cannot be established or refuted.
